review: Reviewer agrees with the writer's reading (श्री = Sītā, as the next verses confirm she comes with him); no change
Reviewer agrees: lines 3–4 left unattributed as the verse names no speaker; the owner may choose Hanumān's thought
Reviewer agrees: तनय is Lakṣmaṇa, Sumitrā's own son; the next dohā goes on with Lakṣmaṇa
Reviewer agrees: the subject of the line is Lakṣmaṇa, so the क्षोभ is his

issue: श्री अनुजजुत: whether श्री here means Sītā
our reading: Sītā (with Śrī, i.e. Sītā, and the younger brother)
alternatives: श्री as an honorific of प्रभु: the glorious Lord with his younger brother

issue: Lines 3–4: whose thought or remark it is
our reading: plain statement following Hanumān falling at Bharata's feet, no speaker named
alternatives: Hanumān's thought (Gita Press)
the narrator's comment

issue: भेटेउ तनय सुमित्राँ: which son
our reading: Sumitrā embraced her son Lakṣmaṇa, knowing his love for Rāma's feet
alternatives: Sumitrā embraced Rāma (as her son), knowing his love/the love of all for his feet

issue: मन कर छोभु न जाइ: whose mind
our reading: Lakṣmaṇa's unrest does not leave him
alternatives: Kaikeyī's agitation does not leave her mind

issue: हरे in line 1: vocative (हे हरे) or verb (हर लिये, carried off) of the beings swayed by māyā
our reading: vocative: O Hari
alternatives: verb: all beings, moving and unmoving, are carried off (captured) under the sway of your māyā

issue: प्रिय संत अनंत सदा: अनंत as the Lord (saints and the Lord are dear) or as 'endlessly' qualifying प्रिय
our reading: saints and the infinite Lord are ever dear to them
alternatives: saints are ever dear to them beyond measure

review: agree: the line allows Bharata as the one who dressed Sugrīva or only as the one who prepared the garments; the meaning keeps the words and the doubt is fairly recorded
agree: भाए can go with लंकापति or with the dressing; the Hindi 'जो … भाते हैं' keeps both open, the alternatives are fairly recorded
agree: पाहि 'protect' as Aṅgada's cry is the usual reading; पाहीं 'near' is fairly recorded
agree: two companions (Śatrughna and Lakṣmaṇa), supported by भाइन्ह सहित in 19.cau3

issue: Who dresses Sugrīva: बसन भरत निज हाथ बनाए may mean Bharata dressed him with his own hands, or that the Lord dressed him in garments Bharata had prepared.
our reading: Sugrīva was dressed first; Bharata arranged the garments with his own hands (left open who put them on).
alternatives: Bharata dressed Sugrīva himself (Gita Press); the Lord dressed him in garments made by Bharata.

issue: लंकापति रघुपति मन भाए: what pleased Śrī Rāma's heart — Vibhīṣaṇa himself (भाए agrees with लंकापति) or the act of dressing him.
our reading: Vibhīṣaṇa, who is dear to Śrī Rāma's heart.
alternatives: The dressing (or the garments) pleased Śrī Rāma (Gita Press).

issue: प्रभु पाही: Sanskrit पाहि 'protect' (Aṅgada's cry), or पाहीं 'near, to' (he fell at the feet beside the Lord).
our reading: A cry: Protect me.
alternatives: He fell at the feet near the Lord (पाहीं = पास).

issue: भरत अनुज सौमित्रि समेता: two companions (the younger brother Śatrughna, and Lakṣmaṇa) or one (the younger brother Saumitri). 19.cau3 भाइन्ह सहित supports two.
our reading: Bharata with his younger brother Śatrughna and Lakṣmaṇa.
alternatives: Bharata with his younger brother, the son of Sumitrā (one person).

review: Agree it is a doubt; the address reading (हे उमा!) is the plain one, since Śiva is narrating here. Keep as recorded.
Agree with our reading (they had been at Agastya's and came from there; the next line's past बरनी supports it). Keep as recorded.

issue: उमा: an address by Śiva to Pārvatī, or one of those who bow to Sītā (adored by Umā, Ramā, Brahmā and others)?
our reading: Address (हे उमा!); रमा names Sītā herself: she is Ramā, adored by Brahmā and the others.
alternatives: Sītā is adored by Umā, Ramā (Lakṣmī), Brahmā and the other gods.

issue: तहाँ रहे सनकादि: had Sanaka and the others been staying with Agastya (and come from there), or is it simply where they live?
our reading: They had been staying with Agastya and came from there; Agastya had told them Rāma's stories.
alternatives: Sanaka and the others were (usually) at Agastya's hermitage.

review: Agree with the writer: Śrī Rāma is the one whose eyes stream (देखि रघुबीरा is the subject of the line); keep as written.
Agree: 'fulfiller of the mind's desires' fits a hymn of petition; pūrṇakāma is a fair alternative for the owner.
Agree: तरन is the boat (MW taraṇa: raft, crossing); 'carries across and is the boat' is a sound reading.
Agree: बिसेषा goes with बिप्र द्रोह; 'to others, and to brāhmaṇas most of all' is the plain reading.

issue: Whose eyes stream and whose body thrills: Śrī Rāma's (seeing the sages' state) or the sages' (describing their state)?
our reading: Śrī Rāma, moved by the sages' state, sheds tears and thrills.
alternatives: The line describes the sages' state itself: tears streaming from their eyes, their bodies thrilled.

issue: मन परिपूरन काम: 'fulfiller of the mind's desires' or 'one whose desires are all fulfilled' (pūrṇakāma).
our reading: You fulfil the longings of the heart.
alternatives: Your every wish is fulfilled (you desire nothing).

issue: तारन तरन: 'one who carries across and the boat (means of crossing)' or 'one who has crossed himself and carries others across'.
our reading: You carry others across and are yourself the boat.
alternatives: Having crossed yourself, you carry others across (Gita Press).

issue: बिप्र द्रोह पर द्रोह बिसेषा: which ill will is 'especially' — to brāhmaṇas, or to others in general?
our reading: Ill will to others, and to brāhmaṇas most of all.
alternatives: Ill will to brāhmaṇas and, above all, to others.

issue: Who is परानंद संदोह: the one who knows the devotee's joy is himself the mass of supreme bliss (the Lord), or one who has attained that bliss?
our reading: only one who is himself a mass of supreme bliss knows his joy (apposition, as the words stand)
alternatives: only one who has attained the supreme bliss (Brahman) knows it; or: the Lord, the mass of supreme bliss, alone knows it

issue: ब्यलीक मद खंडन: 'breaker of false pride' (ब्यलीक qualifying मद) or 'breaker of falsehood and pride' (two objects)
our reading: breaker of falsehood and pride
alternatives: breaker of false (empty) pride

review: Agree it is a genuine doubt; the address 'Satī' fits 56.cau1, keep as is for the owner.
Agree: जान = यान (mount) fits त्रिभुवनपति कर; reading is right.

issue: धन्य सती: सती may be the address 'Satī' (her former name, which Śiva goes on to recall in 56.cau1) or the epithet 'chaste/virtuous one'.
our reading: Address by name: हे सती / Satī.
alternatives: हे पतिव्रता / 'virtuous lady' (sense of the word as an epithet).

issue: जान: read as यान (vehicle, mount: Garuḍa as Viṣṇu's mount) rather than जानना (knows).
our reading: the mount (vāhana) of the Lord of the three worlds.
alternatives: 'one who knows the Lord of the three worlds' (जानना).

review: Agree: परि as the emphatic particle ('only him') fits मिलहिं … तेही best; reading is right.
Agree: the three guṇas, on the model of sannipāta of the three humours, is the plain reading; keep for the owner.

issue: परि in संत बिसुद्ध मिलहिं परि तेही: our word sheet has पड़कर; read as the particle 'only, indeed' (पर/परि)
our reading: pure saints are met only by him on whom Śrī Rāma looks with grace
alternatives: 'saints come and fall in (meet by chance) only with him'; 'but saints meet only him'

issue: गुन कृत सन्यपात: the guṇas of nature (sattva, rajas, tamas) or one's own good qualities
our reading: the delirium brought on by the guṇas (the qualities of nature)
alternatives: delirium caused by one's merits/accomplishments (pride in them)

review: Agree with the writer's doubt and reading (self-address); the owner should decide.
Agree with the writer: 'the full moon in all its sixteen digits' is the plain reading; the doubt can stay for the owner.
Agree with the writer's reading (the home is sorrow itself); a real doubt worth keeping.

issue: तुलसिदास … कस न भजहु: read as Tulasīdāsa addressing himself, or as the poet's signature with भजहु addressed to the listeners ('says Tulasīdāsa, why do you not worship').
our reading: Address to himself: हे तुलसीदास! / Tulasīdāsa, why do you not …
alternatives: Signature: तुलसीदास कहते हैं, भ्रम छोड़कर ऐसे प्रभुको क्यों नहीं भजते? / Tulasīdāsa asks: why do you not …

issue: राकापति षोडस: the full moon 'with its sixteen digits', or literally 'sixteen full moons' rising together.
our reading: The full moon in all its sixteen digits (कलाएँ).
alternatives: Sixteen full moons rise along with the host of stars.

issue: गृहासक्त दुखरूप: दुखरूप may describe the home (attached to the home, which is sorrow itself) or the people (attached to home, themselves miserable).
our reading: The home is sorrow itself.
alternatives: They, attached to home, are wretched / sorrow-laden.

review: Agree with the doubt and with our reading: मागेहु भगति is the subject of मोहि अति भाई in the plain word order; Gita Press refers it to the cleverness. Keep for the owner.
Agree it is a doubt. The bare words say 'he was very hungry'; 'as though' is defensible because it is the child's play (सिसु कौतुक) shown to the mother. Keep for the owner.
Agree with the doubt and with our reading (the slickness water gives does not stay).

issue: What does मोहि अति भाई refer to: the cleverness (चतुराई) or the devotion asked for?
our reading: Your asking for devotion pleased me greatly.
alternatives: This cleverness pleased me greatly.
Devotion, which you asked for, is very dear to me.

issue: चितइ मातु लागी अति भूखा: whether the child is really hungry or only shows his mother that he is.
our reading: He looked at his mother as though very hungry.
alternatives: He looked at his mother: he was very hungry.
He looked at his mother to show that he was very hungry.

issue: जल कै चिकनाई: the simile.
our reading: Devotion without love does not hold, as the slickness water leaves does not last.
alternatives: Like the oiliness of water (which does not exist).
Like the smoothness given by water, which dries off at once.

review: Agree: line 1 reads as the narrator's statement and Garuḍa's words begin at line 2, where ताता addresses Bhuśuṇḍi.
Agree: मतिधीर as an address to Garuḍa fits Bhuśuṇḍi's discourse to him; the general reading stays an alternative.

issue: Who says line 1 (गुर बिनु भव निधि तरइ न कोई…): the narrator's comment on Garuḍa's state, or the opening of Garuḍa's own words (he speaks with ताता in line 2)?
our reading: Line 1 as the narrator's general statement; Garuḍa's speech begins at line 2.
alternatives: Garuḍa's speech begins at line 1.

issue: मतिधीर: an address to Garuḍa ('O steady-minded one') or the subject of a general maxim ('the steady-minded, considering thus…'); भजहु is imperative plural.
our reading: Address to Garuḍa.
alternatives: General: the steady-minded should give up sophistry and worship Śrī Rāma.

review: Agree it is a doubt; leaving guru and disciple unassigned keeps to the words without choosing. Keep for the owner.
Agree: 'kill' is the plain sense of घात करना; 'betray' is the alternative. Keep for the owner.

Disagree with our reading: the plain reading keeps अबला as subject of the whole chhanda (no new subject is named; 102.cau2 then turns to नर). Fixes above apply that reading; the doubt stays for the owner.

issue: गुर सिष बधिर अंध: which of guru and disciple is the deaf one and which the blind; the verse order would make the guru deaf and the disciple blind, Gita Press makes the disciple deaf (does not listen) and the guru blind (has no insight).
our reading: Left unassigned: guru and disciple are like the deaf and the blind; one does not hear, the other does not see.
alternatives: Assign by verse order (guru deaf, disciple blind) or as Gita Press (disciple deaf, guru blind).

issue: अबला governs the first half-line (hair the only ornament, great hunger); whether the rest of the chhanda (poor, sorrowful, much attachment; foolish, wanting happiness, small hard minds) still speaks of women or of people in general.
our reading: Women only for कच भूषन भूरि छुधा; the rest of people in general (102.cau2 goes on with नर).
alternatives: Gita Press reads the whole stanza as about women.

issue: करहिं बिप्र गुर घात: घात may be killing or a treacherous blow / betrayal.
our reading: घात कर देते हैं / kill.
alternatives: 'strike at, betray' a Brahmin or guru.

review: Agree it is a doubt: the accusative आकाशवासं fits a stem आकाशवास 'dwelling in the sky', but वास also means 'garment' (MW), which supports the traditional digambara reading. The plain reading is a sound choice; the owner decides.
Agree: 'महाकालके भी काल' is the usual reading and fits the verse; recording the two-epithet alternative is right.

issue: आकाशवासं: वास read as 'dwelling' (वास, abode) or as 'garment' (वासस्, clothed in the sky, i.e. digambara).
our reading: आकाशमें वास करनेवाले / dwelling in the sky.
alternatives: आकाशको ही वस्त्ररूपमें धारण करनेवाले (दिगम्बर) / clad in the sky.

issue: महाकाल कालं: one epithet 'the death (Kāla) even of Mahākāla', or two epithets 'Mahākāla, Kāla'.
our reading: महाकालके भी काल / the death even of Mahākāla.
alternatives: महाकाल और काल (two names in the list).

review: Reviewer agrees: the plain reading अबला / the female, with no gloss, keeps the verse's words; the next verses themselves make it māyā. Owner to decide
Reviewer agrees: 'the lowest of birds' keeps the sense and avoids the caste word (style sheet §2); the next dohā says it is the crow

issue: अबला: the verse says the female (अबला) is weak by nature; commentators (Gita Press) gloss it as māyā, in contrast with knowledge, dispassion etc. as male, and the next verses go on to māyā and bhakti as female.
our reading: Plain reading: अबला / the female, without a gloss.
alternatives: अबला (माया) / the female (māyā), with the gloss in round brackets.

issue: पच्छी चंडाला: literally 'a cāṇḍāla among birds' (the crow). We render it 'the lowest of birds' rather than keep the caste word.
our reading: पक्षियोंमें सबसे नीच पक्षी / the lowest of birds.
alternatives: चाण्डाल पक्षी (कौआ) / the outcaste among birds.

review: Agree: शम (calm) beside धृति is the better reading; the starter is fortitude and calm. Keep as doubt for the owner.
Agree it is a real doubt: Gita Press takes मुदिता as the churning-vessel; 'with gladness' is the plain reading of मुदिताँ. Keep for the owner.
Agree: ब्रह्म here as the Veda (śabda-brahma) suits the ocean churned for the nectar of the story; keep for the owner.
Agree with our reading: तीनिउ भाई are the three humours called brothers (प्रीति करहिं fits brothers making friends).

issue: धृति सम जावनु: सम may be शम (calm, restraint of mind) or 'like' (fortitude as the starter).
our reading: the starter of fortitude and calm (धैर्य तथा शम).
alternatives: 'with fortitude as the starter' (सम = like).

issue: मुदिताँ मथै: mudita (gladness) may be the manner of churning, the churner, or the churning-vessel.
our reading: with gladness let him churn it.
alternatives: in the vessel of gladness; gladness herself churns it.

issue: ब्रह्म पयोनिधि: ब्रह्म may be Brahman or the Veda (śabda-brahma).
our reading: Brahman, i.e. the Veda, is the ocean.
alternatives: Brahman (the Absolute) as the ocean.

issue: तीनिउ भाई: the three humours called 'brothers', or भाई as an address to Garuḍa (as in 117.cau7, 118.cau4).
our reading: these three brothers (the humours).
alternatives: 'if the three, brother, combine'.

review: Agree: line 2 opens Bhuśuṇḍi's words (cau2 मो पर continues it); naming the speaker follows style §3. Keep the doubt for the owner.
Agree with the doubt; the plain reading (made holy and famous) is acceptable; the other reading (known as purifier of the world) is equally possible.
Agree it is a doubt: Monier-Williams gives kṛtajña both 'knowing what is right, correct in conduct' and 'grateful'; in this list of spiritual types the former may fit better. Owner to decide.
Agree: 'first course' = giving (of दान, भोग, नाश) is the usual reading.

issue: प्रभु मोहि कीन्ह बिदित जग पावन: पावन may be 'holy' (I was made holy, known in the world) or 'purifying' (made known as a purifier of the world).
our reading: The Lord made me holy and famous in the world.
alternatives: The Lord made me known as one who purifies the world (जग पावन together).

issue: कृतग्य (कृतज्ञ) in this list of spiritual types: 'grateful' or 'one who knows (the secret of) action / what ought to be done'.
our reading: कृतज्ञ / the grateful.
alternatives: कर्मके रहस्यके ज्ञाता / those who know the meaning of action (Monier-Williams also gives 'knowing what is right').

issue: Where Bhuśuṇḍi's speech begins: line 2 (महिमा निगम नेति…) runs into 124.cau2 (मो पर कृपा), so it is read as his words, though no verb of speaking is in the verse.
our reading: Line 2 opens his speech: 'फिर वे बोले — / Then he said:'.
alternatives: Line 2 is narration describing Rāma, and the speech begins only with cau2.

issue: प्रथम गति of wealth: read as the first of its three courses (दान, भोग, नाश), i.e. giving.
our reading: The first course, giving (दान).
alternatives: 'Whose course is the best' (used to the best purpose) without naming giving.

issue: सत पंच चौपाईं: read as 'five or seven caupāīs' (सत = सात), or as 'a hundred and five', or with सत पंच as 'true arbiters' (the caupāīs taken as a true guide).
our reading: five or seven (a few) caupāīs.
alternatives: 'a hundred and five caupāīs'; 'knowing the lovely caupāīs to be a true arbiter (सत् पंच)'.

issue: आभीर … स्वपचादि अति अघरूप जे: जे may restrict ('those among them who are sin itself') or describe the whole list ('who are sin itself').
our reading: Restrictive: those among them who are sin itself (the milder sense, per style §2 on groups).
alternatives: Descriptive: the Ābhīras, Yavanas … who are utterly sinful.

issue: राम नमामि ते: ते read as the Sanskrit enclitic 'to you' (address to Rāma) or as 'that' (उन श्रीरामजीको).
our reading: हे राम! मैं आपको नमस्कार करता हूँ / Rāma, I bow to you.
alternatives: 'I bow to that Rāma'.
